s1.syndrome_frame: a chronic skin condition characterized by asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules with a symmetric distribution on the trunk and extremities
salient_findings: red to brown macules and papules on trunk and extremities
key_facts: lesions initially appeared on trunk and spread to upper and proximal lower extremities
face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes are unaffected
some lesions have resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
skin biopsy shows nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils
bone marrow analysis shows hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils
